Under that plan, Warren Buffett becomes chairman emeritus and will remain on the board. His son, Howard G. Buffett, was named chairman, and Susan Decker will remain as lead independent director. Howard Buffett has been on the Berkshire board for 33 years.
The move comes less than a year after Greg Abel became CEO, succeeding Warren Buffett, who served in the role for 60 years.

"Father Time always wins," the 96-year-old billionaire said in a letter to shareholders. "He has, however, been generous with me. He has given me the opportunity to see Berkshire reach a point where I am more confident than ever about what lies ahead."
Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.B) shares edged down 0.1% in Friday premarket trading.
Warren Buffett voiced his support for the Berkshire Hathaway's (BRK.A)(BRK.B) current CEO and chairman, saying part of the reason he feels so good about the change is Abel's leadership.

"My expectations for him were sky high from the start, and he has exceeded them," the elder Buffett said. "He has taken hold of the chief executive officer job in every respect. He has been making the decisions that matter for some time now, and I have not had to think twice about any of them."

Buffett, the company's largest shareholder, announced in July that he's speeding up the pace of annual donations, with the goal of distributing all his remaining Berkshire shares in about eight years.

"Warren’s impact on Berkshire and its owners is without parallel in the history of American business," Abel said in a statement. "The culture Warren built and the values he championed will remain at the heart of Berkshire, and Howard will be their guardian."

Buffett, who took over Berkshire Hathaway in 1965, built the company from a failing textiles business into an insurance powerhouse with a stable of other operating businesses, including railroads, energy, aerospace components, retailing, real estate, truck stops, and homebuilding.
